from_quote: Conditional reduction, independent review pending: let W be a continuous adapted real chordal Loewner driver, W_0=0, with dg_t(z)=2/(g_t(z)-W_t)dt in one usual filtration. For three real marks 0<a<b<c put X=g_t(a)-W_t and Y_i=g_t(b_i)-W_t, b_1=b,b_2=c. On each stopped compact localization with 0<X<Y_1<Y_2 and positive separations, assume BOTH C(X/Y_i) are local martingales, where C(u)=B(1/3,1/3)^(-1) integral_0^u [v(1-v)]^(-2/3)dv. Smooth inversion of the first makes W a semimartingale; the two Ito signed-measure equations force zero finite variation part and local martingale bracket 6dt. If the assumption holds for a countable mark/localization family covering every finite time, W/sqrt(6) is Brownian motion. The square-lattice martingale approximation needed to apply this reduction is unproved in this draft.

to.quote: For 0<u<1 define C(u)=B(1/3,1/3)^(-1) integral_0^u [v(1-v)]^(-2/3)dv, where B(1/3,1/3) is the same integral from 0 to 1. Thus C(0)=0, C(1)=1, C'>0 and C''/C'=2(2u-1)/(3u(1-u)). This definition alone is not a claim that square-lattice crossing probabilities converge to C.

rationale: The two driver tests use the normalized Cardy function and its positive derivative.

from_quote: Conditional counterexample, independent review pending: for kappa>=0, kappa!=6, fix 0<a<b<c and stop in 0<X<Y<Z. Solve locally dX=[2/X-beta]dt-sqrt(kappa)dB and dY=[2/Y-beta]dt-sqrt(kappa)dB with beta=(6-kappa)(1/X+1/Y)/3, X_0=a,Y_0=b. Set W=integral beta dt+sqrt(kappa)B and Z=g_t(c)-W. These X,Y are real Loewner marks for W. For C(u)=B(1/3,1/3)^(-1) integral_0^u [v(1-v)]^(-2/3)dv, C(X/Y) is a local martingale, although W has bracket kappa dt and nonzero drift. The second Cardy observable C(X/Z) has normalized drift (6-kappa)(1/Z-1/Y)/3, which is nonzero. This refutes only one-observable identification, not percolation conformal invariance.

OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status no_resolution_found_in_documented_search; result status attempted_unsolved). Prove that critical bond percolation on Z^2 at p = 1/2 is conformally invariant in the scaling limit (Cardy's formula and convergence of interfaces to SLE(6)), as is known on the triangular lattice by Smirnov. Source: Garban and Steif: Noise sensitivity of Boolean functions and percolation, lecture notes with open problems, Chapter II Section 4, p. 26. Status notes: Bounded search 2026-09-07: no proof of conformal invariance on Z^2 found; the problem is listed as open in Duminil-Copin's ICM 2018 survey as well (dedup with that source).
Posed in Garban and Steif: Noise sensitivity of Boolean functions and percolation, lecture notes with open problems
Current status no_resolution_found_in_documented_search as of 2026-09-07

rationale: This explicitly unproved input concerns identification of the square-bond exploration scaling limit in C0017.

from_quote: Under the standard signed-radian edge parafermion convention F(e)=E[exp(i sigma W(e,e_b))1_{e in gamma}] with sigma in [0,1] satisfying sin(pi sigma/2)=sqrt(q)/2, q=1 gives sigma=1/3, since sin(pi/6)=1/2 and the sine is injective on that branch. The alternative exponent sigma-1 is -2/3. A positive spin 2/3 is not the standard branch; a different winding or conjugation convention must be stated explicitly. This elementary convention correction adds no missing analyticity estimate. Primary support is Definition 3 of Duminil-Copin, arXiv:1208.3787, and equation (1) of Zhou, arXiv:2409.03235v6.

to.quote:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Look for a discrete holomorphic observable on the square lattice analogous to Smirnov's on the triangular lattice. Result: Smirnov's argument needs the three-arm colour-switching symmetry, which on the triangular lattice comes from site self-duality; on Z^2 bond percolation the dual is the shifted square lattice and the exploration interface lives on the medial lattice, where the parafermionic observable F(z) = E[e^{i sigma W(z)} 1_{z on interface}] with spin sigma = ... satisfies only half of the discrete Cauchy-Riemann relations (the contour-integral relations, as for FK models with q not 2). A concrete check: for the q=1 FK model the parafermionic observable has spin sigma = 2/3 and the relation sum over edges around a face vanishes, which gives crossing exponent bounds but not holomorphicity; the missing half is what conformal invariance needs. No new observable found. Obstruction: Only the weak (contour) half of discrete holomorphicity holds for the q=1 parafermion on the square lattice.
